clue.text: Where they lost from start to finish, the French conduct a salvage operation

indicators.note: the opening letter is shifted from the start of the battle name to its finish

parts.note: the French lost the Battle of Crécy to the English in 1346
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone describes rescuing goods where a side was beaten, with the French doing the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they' points ahead to 'the French': the Battle of Crécy (1346) was a famous English victory over France. 'Lost' looks like part of the salvage picture but belongs to the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle is to reclaim waste material for reuse, a kind of salvage work.

clue.text: Having to answer, irresolute person initially dithered

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are unsettled, wavering into a new order
only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: An indecisive person who has to reply hesitates at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to reply, a direct synonym of to answer.

clue.text: Start crossing at caution, clearly before signal to proceed in London

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the amber traffic light signals caution
well can mean clearly or plainly, as in 'well aware'
a green light tells traffic to go

explanation.surface: Advice on crossing a road when the lights turn amber and then green.
explanation.walkthrough: The traffic-light picture misleads: the pieces are simply laid end to end, and 'before' only confirms their order. Camberwell Green is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Camberwell Green is an open space and district in south London, so it is a place found in London.

clue.text: Set to leave drink and start driving

parts.note: congé is a formal word for leave or dismissal
ale is beer

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop drinking and get behind the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something congealed has set solid, as gravy sets when it cools.

clue.text: Odds may be, oddly

parts.note: betting odds of one to one carry a name meaning not odd, which is the paradox the clue enjoys

explanation.definitionFit: Even money odds, an equal stake and return, are called by this word in betting.

clue.text: Deceptive headgear?

parts.note: a flat-crowned hat shares its name with a pastry whose rhyming slang means a lie, so the hat is a 'deceptive' one

explanation.definitionFit: A pork pie is a style of hat, and 'porky pie' is rhyming slang for a lie (British cockney slang).

clue.text: No dilettante was eager to be stretched

parts.note: a professional is the opposite of a dabbling amateur
longed means yearned or was keen

explanation.surface: A serious professional is keen to be pushed further.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolonged means drawn out in time, extended or stretched.

clue.text: Nameless tyrant can become irritable

indicators.note: the remaining letters can turn into a different word by rearranging
name abbreviates to N, and the suffix says it is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: An anonymous despot is liable to lose his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' takes N from TYRANT, leaving TYRAT; 'can become' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for bad-tempered or irritable.

clue.text: Curious dog gets lost

parts.note: take the word Curious, let a dog (cur) go missing from it, and the remaining letters are a written pledge to pay, in plural

explanation.walkthrough: CURIOUS less CUR leaves IOUS, the plural of IOU (I owe you): written promises to repay. 15 down uses that same IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: IOUs are informal written promises to pay a debt, which is what this pair of words names.

clue.text: Pray for space to handle

parts.note: an en is a printing space half the width of an em
to treat someone is to handle or deal with them

explanation.surface: Someone prays for room to cope.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead, the old sense of pray as in 'pray tell'.

clue.text: Father of the House?

parts.note: the title for the longest-serving MP is reread as the founder of the House of Commons itself

explanation.walkthrough: Simon de Montfort's parliament of 1265 is often called the forerunner of the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: This 13th-century earl summoned the first parliament with elected town burgesses, so is called the father of the Commons.

clue.text: With flowing robes, excessive diners conceal their appearance

definitions.text: With flowing robes, excessive diners conceal their appearance

indicators.note: the clue's words keep the answer tucked away across their join

explanation.surface: Big eaters hide their shape under loose robes.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'robES, Excessive' after the R: OBESE. The whole clue also describes overweight diners hiding their figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, which is the appearance excessive diners want to hide.

clue.text: Plot gives point to right-wing policy

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
the Tories are Britain's right-wing Conservative party
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A political scheme gives an edge to Conservative policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyline is the plot of a novel or film.

clue.text: Performing nicely in joint fixture

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: doing means performing an action
well means nicely or satisfactorily

explanation.surface: Someone is doing nicely in a carpentry joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowelling is the wooden pegs used to fix joints together in woodwork.

clue.text: Rude about shape of neck showing bust

indicators.note: the first word wraps around the second piece

parts.note: insolent means rude or impertinent
a V-neck is a garment neckline in that shape

explanation.surface: A rude remark about the neckline of a dress revealing a bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' is not the chest but broke, bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvent means unable to pay debts, informally bust.

clue.text: Miniature donkey's advantage?

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
-et is a suffix making a small version, as in islet

explanation.surface: Is a tiny donkey a benefit?
explanation.walkthrough: The suffix -ET marks a diminutive, so a 'miniature donkey' is ASS + ET.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, an advantage.

clue.text: Ornithological collar?

parts.note: a seabird hung round the neck as in Coleridge's poem, a burden worn like a collar

explanation.walkthrough: In The Rime of the Ancient Mariner the mariner wears the bird he shot round his neck, hence a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: This great seabird, hung round the Ancient Mariner's neck, became a byword for a burden one cannot shed.

clue.text: Handed out, as before under control

parts.note: do. is short for ditto, meaning as before
led means guided or under someone's direction

explanation.surface: Distributed in the same way, under supervision.
explanation.definitionFit: Doled is the past tense of dole, to hand out in portions.

clue.text: Confer dignity on 7 suspect

parts.note: to dub is to confer a knighthood on someone
7 down is answered by IOUs, written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Honouring some doubtful debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down's wordplay gives IOUS (Curious less cur), so it supplies those letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious means doubtful or suspect.

clue.text: Face fungus of American general worn back to front

indicators.note: part from the back of the word is put on at the front

parts.note: burnsides were whiskers named after American Civil War general Ambrose Burnside, who wore them

explanation.surface: Whiskers belonging to a US general are worn the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face fungus' is jocular slang for facial hair. Moving SIDE from the back of BURNSIDES to the front gives SIDEBURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of hair grown down the cheeks, a form of facial hair.

clue.text: Reported morning lack of hilarity

definitions.meaning: a word sounding like morning is mourning, which means grief

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' marks a sound-alike: MOURNING, whose meaning is grief, the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is grief or sorrow, as in mourning, and the opposite of hilarity.

clue.text: Game played with a table leg

indicators.note: the letters are played about with, put in a new order

explanation.surface: A game played with a table leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game in which balls are struck into scoring holes.

clue.text: Infant with hood — that's the bottom line

parts.note: a tot is a small child
Al Capone, the archetypal hood or gangster, gives AL

explanation.surface: A child with a hood on is the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: The total is the figure at the bottom of a column of sums, the bottom line.

clue.text: Record carrier used by old priest with lots

definitions.text: used by old priest with lots

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A record-carrying box used by an ancient priest.
explanation.walkthrough: The ephod held the Urim and Thummim, which priests consulted much as one casts lots.
explanation.definitionFit: The ephod was a vestment of the ancient Israelite high priest, linked with divination by lots.

clue.text: Having arrived at pitch, turned Roger out

indicators.note: the letter goes out of the word, removed

parts.note: Roger is the radio alphabet word for R

explanation.surface: Having reached the field, someone turned Roger away.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument tuned has been brought to the correct musical pitch.

clue.text: Don't spare the horses

parts.note: an old order to a coach driver to go flat out, matched by a motorist's phrase for accelerating

explanation.definitionFit: To open the throttle is to give an engine full power, the modern version of whipping on the horses.

clue.text: Garment sported by model without attachment

parts.note: single means unattached, not in a relationship
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A garment worn by a model who is unattached.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest worn as an undershirt or for athletics.

clue.text: Ship tossed by freak tides leaves off

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about, jumbled by abnormal waves

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A steamer is buffeted by abnormal tides.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to stop, so desists means leaves off.
